---
title: "Tools: cutting and deleting"
description: "The agent tools that split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps, with their arguments, answers and limits."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools cut the timeline: they split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['split', 'split_at_shots', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap']}
/>

## Pick a tool

| You want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Cut clips in two at one time | [`split`](#split) |
| Cut clips at every shot change inside them | [`split_at_shots`](#split_at_shots) |
| Remove clips and leave the gaps | [`delete`](#delete) |
| Remove clips and close the gaps | [`ripple_delete`](#ripple_delete) |
| Remove a stretch of time and close it | [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range) |
| Remove many stretches as one undo step | [`ripple_delete_ranges`](#ripple_delete_ranges) |
| Remove a stretch of time and leave the hole | [`lift_range`](#lift_range) |
| Open empty time | [`insert_time`](#insert_time) |
| Close one gap on a track | [`close_gap`](#close_gap) |

## What these tools share

- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid before anything happens. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
- **Locked tracks** never move, and a stretch of time removed from the timeline leaves them alone. Lock a track to keep it out of a timeline-wide edit.
- **Markers** stay at their times under every ripple. Only `insert_time` moves them.
- **Linked clips.** A clip and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) stay together, as each tool below says. A partner on a locked track is never pulled in.

## `split`

Cuts clips in two at one time. The second piece plays on from where the first stopped, so the join can't be seen.

It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where to cut. Left out, the playhead. |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to cut, at least one. Left out, every clip on an unlocked track that `at` falls inside, as the menu item does with nothing selected. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Each piece keeps the actions on its side, and an action that crosses the cut becomes two. The first piece keeps the clip's id and any transition into it. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut. Its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track and `at` falls inside it, and the new halves are linked to each other.

**Answers** `new_clips`, the second pieces.

**Changes nothing** for a named clip `at` isn't strictly inside, which is skipped. If no clip can be cut, the answer is "Split made no change". An unknown clip id is an error.

## `split_at_shots`

Cuts clips of a video file at every hard cut inside the part of the file they play, as one undo step named Split at Shot Changes. It shows no sheet.

It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), which says what counts as a hard cut.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to split. An empty list is an error. Left out, every clip of a video file on an unlocked track in what's open. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |

It has no `scope` argument. It works in the nest [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/) has open, or on the timeline.

A clip it can cut is a clip of a video file with its picture on. Any other clip you name is reported under `skipped`. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut, and its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track.

The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload, and they're kept in the project's cache, so a second call answers from it. Each cut is worked out through the clip's speed, ramp and reversal, and lands on the frame grid. A cut within one frame of either end of the clip isn't made. To read the cuts without splitting, use [`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

**Answers:**

| Key | 

... [5780 characters truncated] ...

ded to the frame grid and put in order, so a reversed pair is the same range. Pairs that touch or overlap then merge, and what's left is cut from right to left, each cut as `ripple_delete_range` makes it. So every time you send is a time in the project as you read it, and this isn't the same as calling `ripple_delete_range` once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two.

**Answers** `new_clips`, the pieces left after each range of any clip cut at a range's end.

**Won't run** when `ranges` is empty, which is an error, or when a shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline. A list whose pairs are all empty changes nothing. Each cut can add a clip, so a list that would pass 4,096 clips is an error and nothing is cut.

## `lift_range`

Cuts a stretch of time out and leaves the hole. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range and what's between is removed, and nothing moves. Use it when a mix or a caption track is already timed.

It mirrors <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) set and nothing selected. See [Lift a range](/editing/delete-clips/#lift-a-range).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. To close the hole as well, use [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range).

**Answers** `new_clips`, the piece left after the range of any clip cut at `to`. The undo step is named Lift.

**Won't run** when `to` isn't after `from`, which is an error. A range with nothing an unlocked track can give up changes nothing.

## `insert_time`

Opens empty time: every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later, and so does every marker at or after that point.

It has no menu item or gesture of its own. See [Insert time](/editing/close-gaps/#insert-time).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the gap opens. |
| `length` | integer, ticks | Yes | How much room to open. It must come to at least one frame. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Clips that cross `at` stay in place, so nothing is cut. To open a gap inside a clip, call [`split`](#split) first. A moved clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it. No marker can land on another, because they all move by the same length.

**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. The undo step is named Insert Time.

**Won't run** when `length` is zero or negative once it's on the frame grid, which is an error.

## `close_gap`

Closes the empty stretch on a track that contains a time. Everything from the far side of the gap, on every unlocked track, slides left by the gap's length.

It mirrors double-clicking a gap in a lane, and **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. See [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track the gap is on. |
| `at` | integer, ticks | Yes | A time inside the gap. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |

title: "Tools: cutting and deleting"
description: "The agent tools that split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps, with their arguments, answers and limits."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools cut the timeline: they split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['split', 'split_at_shots', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap']}
/>

## Pick a tool

| You want to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Cut clips in two at one time | [`split`](#split) |
| Cut clips at every shot change inside them | [`split_at_shots`](#split_at_shots) |
| Remove clips and leave the gaps | [`delete`](#delete) |
| Remove clips and close the gaps | [`ripple_delete`](#ripple_delete) |
| Remove a stretch of time and close it | [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range) |
| Remove many stretches as one undo step | [`ripple_delete_ranges`](#ripple_delete_ranges) |
| Remove a stretch of time and leave the hole | [`lift_range`](#lift_range) |
| Open empty time | [`insert_time`](#insert_time) |
| Close one gap on a track | [`close_gap`](#close_gap) |

## What these tools share

- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid before anything happens. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
- **Locked tracks** never move, and a stretch of time removed from the timeline leaves them alone. Lock a track to keep it out of a timeline-wide edit.
- **Markers** stay at their times under every ripple. Only `insert_time` moves them.
- **Linked clips.** A clip and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) stay together, as each tool below says. A partner on a locked track is never pulled in.

## `split`

Cuts clips in two at one time. The second piece plays on from where the first stopped, so the join can't be seen.

It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where to cut. Left out, the playhead. |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to cut, at least one. Left out, every clip on an unlocked track that `at` falls inside, as the menu item does with nothing selected. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Each piece keeps the actions on its side, and an action that crosses the cut becomes two. The first piece keeps the clip's id and any transition into it. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut. Its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track and `at` falls inside it, and the new halves are linked to each other.

**Answers** `new_clips`, the second pieces.

**Changes nothing** for a named clip `at` isn't strictly inside, which is skipped. If no clip can be cut, the answer is "Split made no change". An unknown clip id is an error.

## `split_at_shots`

Cuts clips of a video file at every hard cut inside the part of the file they play, as one undo step named Split at Shot Changes. It shows no sheet.

It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), which says what counts as a hard cut.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to split. An empty list is an error. Left out, every clip of a video file on an unlocked track in what's open. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |

It has no `scope` argument. It works in the nest [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/) has open, or on the timeline.

A clip it can cut is a clip of a video file with its picture on. Any other clip you name is reported under `skipped`. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut, and its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track.

The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload, and they're kept in the project's cache, so a second call answers from it. Each cut is worked out through the clip's speed, ramp and reversal, and lands on the frame grid. A cut within one frame of either end of the clip isn't made. To read the cuts without splitting, use [`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

**Answers:**

| Key | 

... [5780 characters truncated] ...

ded to the frame grid and put in order, so a reversed pair is the same range. Pairs that touch or overlap then merge, and what's left is cut from right to left, each cut as `ripple_delete_range` makes it. So every time you send is a time in the project as you read it, and this isn't the same as calling `ripple_delete_range` once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two.

## `lift_range`

Cuts a stretch of time out and leaves the hole. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range and what's between is removed, and nothing moves. Use it when a mix or a caption track is already timed.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |

| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. To close the hole as well, use [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range).

**Answers** `new_clips`, the piece left after the range of any clip cut at `to`. The undo step is named Lift.

**Won't run** when `to` isn't after `from`, which is an error. A range with nothing an unlocked track can give up changes nothing.

## `insert_time`

Opens empty time: every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later, and so does every marker at or after that point.

It has no menu item or gesture of its own. See [Insert time](/editing/close-gaps/#insert-time).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the gap opens. |
| `length` | integer, ticks | Yes | How much room to open. It must come to at least one frame. |
| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

**Won't run** when `length` is zero or negative once it's on the frame grid, which is an error.

## `close_gap`

| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

The gap runs between the nearest clip edges on that track, or from the start of the timeline when no clip comes before it. A gap closes fully or not at all, so a smaller gap never means it stopped part-way.

**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. A clip that slides onto a neighbour by an amount the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows gets a Cross Dissolve.

**Won't run** in these cases. Each message names what's in the way, and nothing moves:

- `at` is on a clip, so it isn't in a gap.
- No clip on the track starts after `at`.
- The track is locked. Its own clips are the ones that would stay behind.
- The shift would break the overlap rule on a track it moves.

7	
8	These tools make more of what's already on the timeline. They copy clips, copy one clip's settings onto others, and group clips into one clip or take that group apart.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['duplicate', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'nest', 'unnest']} />
11	
12	## What these tools share
13	
14	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
15	- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
16	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
17	
18	## The payload
19	
20	`paste` and `paste_attributes` both take a `payload`, an object in the form **Edit ▸ Copy** puts on the clipboard. No tool reads the clipboard, so an agent builds its own from what `get_project` lists:
21	
22	```json
23	{
24	  "clips": [],
25	  "media": [],
26	  "nests": []
27	}
28	```
29	
30	| Key | Required | What it holds |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `clips` | Yes, at least one | Clip objects as `get_project` lists them, each with its `track` changed as below. |
33	| `media` | When a clip uses a file | The media rows those clips use, as `get_project` lists them. |
34	| `nests` | When a clip shows a nest | The nests those clips show, and any nest inside them, as `get_project` lists them. |
35	
36	Two things differ from what `get_project` gives you:
37	
38	- **A clip's `track` is a depth, not a track id.** 0 is the front-most lane, 1 the lane behind it, and so on, because a track id means nothing in another project.
39	- **Ids are only used inside the payload**, to tie clips to their media and nests. Everything that lands gets a fresh id, so a payload can be pasted again and again, into any project.
40	
41	Keys Frame Job doesn't know are ignored. A payload that isn't an object, or has no clips, is an error.
42	
43	## `duplicate`
44	
45	Copies clips onto their own tracks, placed straight after the span the originals cover, so a selection keeps its internal timing.
46	
47	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>). See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
48	
49	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |

52	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |

54

57	**Answers** `new_clips`, the copies.

72	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
73	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

76	
77	- **Media** is matched to this project by path. A row the project already has is reused, and one it lacks is added. Only files the pasted clips use come across.

80	- **Missing tracks** are added at the back.
81	- **No room:** a clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped. A smaller overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.

104	| `payload` | object | Yes | Holds the clip to copy from. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
105	| `groups` | array of strings | No | Which groups travel: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`. Left out, each of the first four that both clips have, and never `graphic`. An empty list is an error. |

108	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
109

111	
112	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
113	| --- | --- | --- |
114	| `video` | Every picture setting, position and scale included. | An adjustment clip keeps its own qualifier when the copied clip isn't an adjustment clip. A picture clip takes no qualifier. |
115	| `audio` | Every sound setting, mute and keep pitch included. | Nothing. |
116	| `text` | Every text setting. | Its words and their timings. |

121	
122	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`, and `new_media` when a look's `.cube` file was added.
123

125	
126	- `groups` is empty or names something else.
127	- Without `skip_missing`, a named group is one the copied clip lacks, or a target lacks. The message names the group or the clip.
128	- Without `skip_missing`, `graphic` meets a clip drawn by another graphic. The message names both.
129	- A copied value is one the inspector wouldn't accept on that clip. See [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops).
130	
131	When the paste would leave every clip as it was, the answer is "Paste Attributes made no change".
132	
133	## `nest`
134	
135	Collapses clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.
136	
137	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Nest** (<kbd>⌘G</kbd>). See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
138	
139	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
140	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
141	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to group, at least one. |
142	| `name` | string | No | What to call the group. Left out or blank, `Nest <n>`. |
143	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
144	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
145	
146	The clips move whole, keeping their ids, settings, actions, transitions, relative times and stacking, with the earliest starting at 0 inside the nest. A linked partner on an unlocked track goes in with its clip. The nest clip lands on the front-most track the clips were on, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. If those tracks include a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), it lands on the front-most track that isn't one, or the front-most track when all of them are.
147	
148	The nest's canvas is fixed at the project's current size, so a later `set_canvas` can't re-lay out what's inside.
149	
150	**Answers** `new_clips`, which is the nest clip, and `new_tracks`, the nest's own tracks. `get_project` lists the group under `nests`, and the nest clip's `source.project` gives its id, which is what `scope` takes.
151	
152	**Won't run** when:
153	
154	- The clips include an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), which can't go inside a nest.
155	- The nest clip would overlap something unselected by more than the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
156	- It would pass 64 tracks, counting the nest's own, or eight levels of nesting.
157	
158	`clips` holding only a clip that's already a nest changes nothing. An empty list or an unknown clip id is an error.
159	
160	## `unnest`
161	
162	Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes.
163	
164	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>). See [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest).
165	
166	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
167	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The nest clip to open. |
169	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
170	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
171	
172	It's the inverse of `nest`, apart from the ids, which are all fresh. Clips land at the nest clip's start plus their own, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's own, and missing tracks are added behind it. A clip the overlap rule won't allow goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped.
173	
174	A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents gives all of them back, because trimming a nest hides what's inside and doesn't cut it. When another clip still shows the same nest, the nest stays for that clip.
175	
176	**Answers** `new_clips`, the returned clips, and `new_tracks` when any were added.
177	
178	**Won't run** on a clip that isn't a nest, which is an error.

2	title: "Tools: speed and time"
3	description: "The agent tools that change a clip's speed, ramp it, retime a stretch of the timeline, play a clip backwards and hold a frame, with their arguments, answers and limits."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools change how time passes in a clip: its rate, a ramp between rates, a whole stretch of the timeline played faster or slower, the direction it plays, and a held frame.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame']} />
11	
12	## Pick a tool
13	
14	| You want to | Use |
15	| --- | --- |
16	| Play one clip at a rate, or fit it to a length | [`set_speed`](#set_speed) |
17	| Make a clip end at a time by changing its speed | [`rate_stretch`](#rate_stretch) |
18	| Ease a clip from one rate to another | [`add_speed_ramp`](#add_speed_ramp) |
19	| Play a stretch of the whole timeline faster or slower | [`retime_range`](#retime_range) |
20	| Play a clip backwards | [`set_reversed`](#set_reversed) |
21	| Hold one frame | [`freeze_frame`](#freeze_frame) |
22	
23	## What these tools share
24	
25	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
26	- **One call is one undo step.**
27	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
28	- **Rates** run from ×0.1 to ×1000, where 1 is normal speed. See each tool for what it does with a rate outside that.
29	
30	### Above ×12 the sound is left out
31	
32	A clip playing above ×12 is silent in the preview and the export, with or without keep pitch. A person is asked first. A tool call never asks: the edit lands, and the answer gains two keys. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
33	
34	| Key | What it holds |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `audio_left_out` | The ids of the clips this edit took past ×12. |
37	| `audio_note` | A sentence saying those clips are now silent. |
38	
39	Only a clip with its sound on, using a file that has sound, counts, and only when this edit took it over the line. A clip already above ×12 isn't reported again. On a ramped clip, the fastest rate in the ramp is the one that counts.
40	
41	### Captions move with the speech
42	
43	`set_speed`, `rate_stretch` and `add_speed_ramp` re-time captions on a Captions track that lie wholly inside a clip with sound, in the same undo step, whose name gains "and Re-time Captions". See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
44	
45	| Key | What it holds |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `captions_retimed` | The caption clips that moved. |
48	| `captions_removed` | The caption clips whose speech the clip no longer plays. |
49	
50	### Linked clips
51	
52	A clip linked to its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) can't change speed or direction, because the other half would have to change with it. `set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_reversed` and `retime_range` all stop with "clip 12 is linked to clip 13: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". Call `attach_audio` first.
53	
54	## `set_speed`
55	
56	Changes a clip's playback rate, or fits it to a length. The clip keeps its start and its length follows the rate, so a faster clip can leave a gap after it. Later clips don't move.
57	
58	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Speed…**. See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/). With `duration` it mirrors **Fit to** in the Speed section. See [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/).
59	
60	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
61	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
62	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to change. |
63	| `rate` | number | One of `rate` or `duration` | 1 is normal, 2 twice as fast and half as long, 0.5 slow motion. From 0.1 to 1000. |
64	| `duration` | integer, ticks | One of `rate` or `duration` | The length to fit the clip to, instead of a rate. |
65	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keep the sound's pitch at the new speed. Left out, the clip's setting stays. |
66	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
67	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
68	
69	A rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000 is brought inside that range, not turned down. That goes for the rate a `duration` needs too, so a clip can end up a different length from the one you asked for. The new length lands on the frame grid and never runs past what the file holds at that rate. Actions keep their place, as fractions of the clip's length.
70	
71	On a clip with a speed ramp, every rate in the ramp scales together, so it keeps its shape. The scale stops where any of its rates would pass the limits, so the clip's rate can stop short of the one you asked for. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
72	
73	**Answers** the usual keys, with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`, and `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed`, when they apply. The undo step is named Speed.
74	
75	**Won't run** when:
76	
77	- Both or neither of `rate` and `duration` are given, which is an error. So `keep_pitch` can't be sent alone.
78	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip. Text, shapes, images, stills, graphics and nests are errors.
79	- `rate` or `duration` is zero or negative, which is an error. A `duration` that rounds to zero on the frame grid counts as zero.
80	- The clip is [linked](#linked-clips).
81	- A slowed clip would run into the next clip by more than the [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a transition.
82	
83	## `rate_stretch`
84	
85	Makes a clip end at a new time by changing its speed instead of trimming it. Everything the clip shows still plays, faster or slower.
86	
87	It mirrors <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging a clip's end edge. See [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/).
88	
89	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
90	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
91	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to stretch. |
92	| `to_end` | integer, ticks | Yes | The clip's new end on the timeline. |
93	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
94	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
95	
96	Actions keep their place, as fractions of the clip's length. A speed ramp on the clip scales with it and keeps its shape.
97	
98	**Answers** the usual keys, with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`, and `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed`, when they apply. The undo step is named Rate Stretch.
99	
100	**Changes nothing** when the new length would be under one frame, or the stretch would take any rate past ×0.1 or ×1000. Unlike a drag, it doesn't stop at the last length that worked.
101	
102	**Won't run** when:
103	
104	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip. A text, shape, image or freeze clip has no source to stretch, which is an error.
105	- The clip is [linked](#linked-clips).
106	- The stretch would run into the next clip by more than the overlap rule allows.
107	
108	## `add_speed_ramp`
109	
110	Makes a speed ramp preset on a clip in one step, out of ordinary speed actions. The clip keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source.
111	
112	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**, but it isn't tied to the in and out range. See [Make a ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/).
113	
114	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
115	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
116	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to ramp. |
117	| `shape` | string | Yes | `ramp_up`, `ramp_down`, `speed_dip` or `speed_burst`. |
118	| `rate` | number | Yes | The rate to ramp to, from 0.1 to 1000. Outside that it's brought inside. Zero or less is an error. |
119	| `from` | integer, ticks | No | Where the span starts, measured from the clip's own start. Give it with `to`. |
120	| `to` | integer, ticks | No | Where the span ends, in clip time. Give it with `from`. With neither, the span is the whole clip. |
121	| `curve` | string | No | How each new action eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. Default `ease_in_out`. |
122	| `hold` | number | No | `speed_dip` and `speed_burst` only: how much of the span the hold at `rate` takes, from 0 to 0.9. Default 0.5. 0 makes the two ramps meet. |
123	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
124	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
125	
126	The base rate is the rate the clip plays at `from` before the edit. After an earlier speed action, that's the action's end rate.
127	
128	| `shape` | What it makes | `rate` must be |
129	| --- | --- | --- |
130	| `ramp_up` | One action over the span, from the base rate to `rate`, which then holds. | Above the base rate |
131	| `ramp_down` | The same, slowing down. | Below the base rate |
132	| `speed_burst` | Two actions: up to `rate` at the start of the span and back to the base rate at its end, holding `rate` between them. | Above the base rate |
133	| `speed_dip` | The same two, slowing down and coming back. | Below the base rate |
134	
135	**Answers** `clip`, `new_actions` with the new actions' ids, and `audio_left_out`, `audio_note`, `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` when they apply. The undo step is named for the shape, such as Speed Dip.
136	
137	**Errors** come first, and name the argument:
138	
139	- The clip isn't a video or audio file clip.
140	- Only one of `from` and `to` is given, `to` isn't after `from`, or `from` is negative.
141	- `hold` is given with `ramp_up` or `ramp_down`.
142	
143	**Won't run** in these cases, checked in this order. Each message says why:
144	
145	| What stops it | What to do |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| The span runs past the clip's end. | Shorten the span. |
148	| The span overlaps an action on the clip, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The message names it, and it's never replaced. | Pick a clear span, or move or remove the action. |
149	| A dip or burst span is under two frames. | Widen the span. |
150	| `rate` is on the wrong side of the base rate. The message gives the base rate. | Change `rate` or `shape`. |
151	| The clip is [linked](#linked-clips). | Call `attach_audio` first. |
152	| The clip would read past the end of its media. The message names the largest rate that fits, or says none does. | Use that rate, or shorten the span. |
153	
154	## `retime_range`
155	
156	Plays a stretch of the timeline faster or slower on every unlocked track, and moves everything after it up or back to stay in step.
157	
158	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**, but it takes its own times and doesn't read the in and out range. See [Retime a range](/speed/retime-range/).
159	
160	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
161	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
162	| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
163	| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
164	| `rate` | number | Yes | 2 is twice as fast and the range half as long, 0.5 half speed. From 0.1 to 1000. |
165	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keep the sound's pitch at the new speed for every video and audio file clip in the range. Left out, each stays as it is. |
166	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
167	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
168	
169	Each clip across `from` or `to` is cut there, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split) cuts it. Each video or audio file clip inside plays at its own rate times `rate`, and a speed ramp scales whole. Text, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed the same way. Actions keep their place. Markers inside move with the picture, markers after it move with the rest, and a linked partner of a moved clip moves with it.
170	
171	Inside a nest, the nest's own tracks are retimed and no marker moves. Unlike `set_speed`, `rate_stretch` and `add_speed_ramp`, it doesn't re-time captions on a Captions track, and it stops at a caption page with timed words. A `rate` of 1 changes nothing.
172	
173	**Answers** `new_clips`, the pieces the cuts made, and `audio_left_out` and `audio_note` when a clip crosses ×12. The undo step is named Retime Range.
174	
175	**Errors:** `to` isn't after `from`, or `rate` is missing, zero or negative.
176	
177	**Won't run** in these cases, and nothing changes. A clip only has to overlap the range to count.
178	
179	| What stops it | What to do |
180	| --- | --- |
181	| `rate` is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. This one isn't brought inside the range. | Pick a rate inside it. |
182	| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
183	| A locked track has a clip that ends after `from`. | Unlock the track, or move `from` past that clip. |
184	| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
185	| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
186	| The range touches a [linked](#linked-clips) clip. | Call `attach_audio` first. |
187	| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
188	| Two markers would land on one time. | Move one of them first. |
189	| A clip would play past ×0.1 or ×1000. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
190	| A clip would last under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |
191	
192	## `set_reversed`
193	
194	Plays a clip back to front, or forward again. It isn't a toggle: you say which way it plays.
195	
196	It mirrors the **Reverse** checkbox in the Clip tab's Timing section. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
197	
198	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
199	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
200	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to change. |
201	| `reversed` | boolean | Yes | True plays it backwards, false forwards again. |
202	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
203	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
204	
205	Nothing on the timeline moves. The clip keeps its start, its length and its in point, and the in point is measured in the direction the clip plays, so reversing a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file.
206	
207	:::caution
208	A clip plays backwards from a rendered copy of its file. In a project with a window, the Reversing sheet appears to make the copy the first time. Until the copy exists the clip shows a [slate](/speed/reverse/#the-slate), and an export writes the slate. A project open with no window shows no sheet and starts no render, so its reversed clips stay on the slate until the project is opened in a window.
209	:::
210	
211	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. The undo step is named Reverse. A clip already playing that way changes nothing.
212	
213	**Won't run** when the clip isn't a video or audio file clip, which is an error, or when it's [linked](#linked-clips).
214	
215	## `freeze_frame`
216	
217	Holds one frame. The clip is split at the moment, a gap opens across every unlocked track, and a still of that exact frame fills it, so the rest of the cut stays in step.
218	
219	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (<kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>), but it can hold any moment of a clip without moving the playhead, for any length. See [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
220	
221	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
222	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
223	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to freeze. |
224	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | The moment to hold, on the timeline. Left out, the playhead. |
225	| `duration` | integer, ticks | No | How long to hold, at least one frame. Default 2 s, which is 1200000. |
226	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
227	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
228	
229	The still takes the clip's picture settings as they stand at that moment. It has no sound, no actions and no entrance or exit motion. Markers at or after `at` move with the gap. At a clip's very start or end there's nothing to split, and the still goes in without a cut. To change the frame a freeze holds afterwards, use `slip` on it.
230	
231	**Answers** `new_clips`, which holds the still, and the clip's second piece when there was a split. The undo step is named Freeze Frame.
232	
233	**Won't run** when:
234	
235	- The clip isn't a video file clip with a picture, which is an error. An audio-only clip, text, a shape, an image, a graphic, a nest or another still can't be frozen.
236	- The clip doesn't cover `at`, which is an error.
237	- `duration` comes to under one frame on the frame grid, which is an error.
238	- The still would break the overlap rule. This happens inside a [transition](/motion/transitions/) and on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), whose clips can't move out of the still's way.

60	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), which says what counts as a hard cut.
61	
62	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
63	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
64	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to split. An empty list is an error. Left out, every clip of a video file on an unlocked track in what's open. |
65	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
66	
67	It has no `scope` argument. It works in the nest [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/) has open, or on the timeline.
68	
69	A clip it can cut is a clip of a video file with its picture on. Any other clip you name is reported under `skipped`. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut, and its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track.
70	
71	The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload, and they're kept in the project's cache, so a second call answers from it. Each cut is worked out through the clip's speed, ramp and reversal, and lands on the frame grid. A cut within one frame of either end of the clip isn't made. To read the cuts without splitting, use [`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
72	
73	**Answers:**
74	
75	| Key | What it holds |
76	| --- | --- |
77	| `cuts` | One `{clip, at}` for each clip that was cut, `at` being a list of timeline ticks. |
78	| `added` | How many clips the splits made, linked partners included. |
79	| `skipped` | The ids of named clips it couldn't cut. |
80	| `cached` | True when nothing had to be read first. |
81	| `new_clips` | The new clips' ids. The original id keeps the first piece. |
82	
83	With no cut inside any clip, `added` is 0, a `note` says so, and there's no undo step.
84	
85	**Won't run** in these cases, and nothing is split:
86	
87	- No clip qualifies. The message says none of the clips shows a moving picture.
88	- The splits would pass 4,096 clips. The message gives how many it would add, counting linked partners, and how many fit.
89	- The analysis takes longer than 60 s. What was covered is kept, so call again to carry on.
90	- The analysis failed, was stopped, or the file can't be read.
91	- The project or the open nest changed during the wait. Call again.

93	## `delete`
94	
95	Removes clips and leaves the gaps. Nothing else moves.
96	
97	It mirrors <kbd>⌫</kbd> and **Edit ▸ Delete** with clips selected. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/#delete-clips-and-leave-a-gap).
98	
99	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
100	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
101	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to remove, at least one. |
102	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
103	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
104	
105	A clip you name on a locked track is still removed. A picture takes its linked sound with it, unless the sound's track is locked. A linked sound named alone goes alone, and the picture stays, silent.
106	
107	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.

109	## `ripple_delete`
110	
111	Removes clips and closes each hole: everything that starts after a removed clip's span, on every unlocked track, slides left by that span's length.
112	
113	It mirrors <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** with clips selected. See [Ripple delete clips](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-clips).
114	
115	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
116	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
117	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to remove, at least one. |
118	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
120	
121	A clip you name on a locked track is still removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move. Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you name. A clip on another track that crosses a removed span stays where it is, and two removed clips that touch leave one hole. A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [How a ripple closes holes](/editing/delete-clips/#how-a-ripple-closes-holes).
122	
123	**Won't run** when the shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can. The message names both clips, and nothing moves. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
124	
125	## `ripple_delete_range`
126	
127	Cuts one stretch of time out of the timeline and closes it. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what's between is removed, and the rest slides left by the range's length.
128	
129	It mirrors <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> with an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) set and nothing selected. See [Ripple delete a range](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-a-range).
130	
131	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
132	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
133	| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
134	| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
135	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
136	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
137	
138	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
139	
140	**Answers** `new_clips`, the piece left after the range of any clip cut at `to`. That piece has a new id.
141	
142	**Won't run** when `to` isn't after `from`, which is an error, or when the shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline. The undo step is named Ripple Delete.
143	
144	## `ripple_delete_ranges`

2	title: "Tools: copying and nesting"
3	description: "The agent tools that duplicate and paste clips, copy one clip's look onto others, and group clips into a nest, with their arguments, answers and limits."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools make more of what's already on the timeline. They copy clips, copy one clip's settings onto others, and group clips into one clip or take that group apart.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['duplicate', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'nest', 'unnest']} />
11	
12	## What these tools share
13	
14	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
15	- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
16	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
17	
18	## The payload
19	
20	`paste` and `paste_attributes` both take a `payload`, an object in the form **Edit ▸ Copy** puts on the clipboard. No tool reads the clipboard, so an agent builds its own from what `get_project` lists:
21	
22	```json
23	{
24	  "clips": [],
25	  "media": [],
26	  "nests": []
27	}
28	```
29	
30	| Key | Required | What it holds |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `clips` | Yes, at least one | Clip objects as `get_project` lists them, each with its `track` changed as below. |
33	| `media` | When a clip uses a file | The media rows those clips use, as `get_project` lists them. |
34	| `nests` | When a clip shows a nest | The nests those clips show, and any nest inside them, as `get_project` lists them. |
35	
36	Two things differ from what `get_project` gives you:
37	
38	- **A clip's `track` is a depth, not a track id.** 0 is the front-most lane, 1 the lane behind it, and so on, because a track id means nothing in another project.
39	- **Ids are only used inside the payload**, to tie clips to their media and nests. Everything that lands gets a fresh id, so a payload can be pasted again and again, into any project.
40	
41	Keys Frame Job doesn't know are ignored. A payload that isn't an object, or has no clips, is an error.
42	
43	## `duplicate`
44	
45	Copies clips onto their own tracks, placed straight after the span the originals cover, so a selection keeps its internal timing.
46	
47	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>). See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
48	
49	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
51	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to copy, at least one. |
52	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
53	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
54	
55	Follow it with `move_clip` to put the copies anywhere else. A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track is copied too, and the two copies are linked to each other. A copy of a nest clip shows the same nest as the original. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
56	
57	**Answers** `new_clips`, the copies.
58	
59	**Won't run** when a copy would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) on its track. Later clips aren't pushed out of the way. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
60	
61	## `paste`
62	
63	Places a [payload](#the-payload)'s clips on the timeline. The earliest clip lands exactly at `at`, and the others keep their distance from it, so a copied arrangement pastes back intact.
64	
65	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste** (<kbd>⌘V</kbd>), without touching the clipboard. See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
66	
67	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
68	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
69	| `payload` | object | Yes | The clips to place. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
70	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where the earliest clip lands. Left out, the playhead. |
71	| `track` | integer | No | The track id where depth 0 lands, and the other depths follow behind it. Left out, the front-most track. |
72	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
73	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
74	
75	What Frame Job does to make the clips fit:
76	
77	- **Media** is matched to this project by path. A row the project already has is reused, and one it lacks is added. Only files the pasted clips use come across.
78	- **Nests** are always copied, never matched, so editing one copy afterwards leaves the other alone. Copy itself writes no `nests` key, so a nest clip on the clipboard can't be pasted, but a payload that carries the nest can.
79	- **Times** are rounded to this project's frame grid.
80	- **Missing tracks** are added at the back.
81	- **No room:** a clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped. A smaller overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
82	- **Links:** a linked pair in the payload lands as a linked pair. A clip whose partner isn't in the payload loses its link.
83	
84	**Answers** `new_clips`, and `new_tracks` and `new_media` when any were added.
85	
86	**Won't run** in these cases, and a paste lands whole or not at all:
87	
88	- The payload isn't an object, has no clips, or doesn't match the clip form.
89	- A clip uses a file or shows a nest the payload doesn't carry, or a media row has an empty path.
90	- A value is out of range. The message names the clip by its id in the payload.
91	- `track` doesn't exist in this project.
92	- A clip's depth is past the 64-track limit, or the paste would pass 64 tracks or 4,096 clips.
93	- It would put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) inside a nest.
94	
95	## `paste_attributes`
96	
97	Copies one clip's settings onto other clips. It reads only the payload's earliest clip: the one with the earliest start, then the front-most, then the lower id. Never assume that's the first clip in the array.
98	
99	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) and, with `groups` set to `["graphic"]` and `skip_missing` on, **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
100	
101	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
102	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
103	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. |
104	| `payload` | object | Yes | Holds the clip to copy from. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
105	| `groups` | array of strings | No | Which groups travel: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`. Left out, each of the first four that both clips have, and never `graphic`. An empty list is an error. |
106	| `skip_missing` | boolean | No | Only with `groups`. On, a group the payload's clip lacks is dropped, and a clip that can't take a group is skipped for it. Default off. |
107	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
108	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
109	
110	Each group replaces the target's whole group, and nothing is merged:
111	
112	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
113	| --- | --- | --- |
114	| `video` | Every picture setting, position and scale included. | An adjustment clip keeps its own qualifier when the copied clip isn't an adjustment clip. A picture clip takes no qualifier. |
115	| `audio` | Every sound setting, mute and keep pitch included. | Nothing. |
116	| `text` | Every text setting. | Its words and their timings. |
117	| `shape` | Every shape setting. | Its kind, width, height, and `from` and `to` points. |
118	| `graphic` | The graphic's properties, whole, onto clips drawn by the same graphic. | Its name, size, in point and length, and any property an action on that clip animates that the copied clip lacks. |
119	
120	Speed, whether the picture and sound are on, actions, the transition, the clip's name and its label never travel. A [look](/color/luts/) brings its `.cube` file by path when the payload's `media` carries it, and a look whose file isn't there comes across as no look.
121	
122	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`, and `new_media` when a look's `.cube` file was added.
123	
124	**Won't run** in these cases, and no clip changes:
125	
126	- `groups` is empty or names something else.
127	- Without `skip_missing`, a named group is one the copied clip lacks, or a target lacks. The message names the group or the clip.
128	- Without `skip_missing`, `graphic` meets a clip drawn by another graphic. The message names both.
129	- A copied value is one the inspector wouldn't accept on that clip. See [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops).
130	
131	When the paste would leave every clip as it was, the answer is "Paste Attributes made no change".
132	
133	## `nest`
134	
135	Collapses clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.
136	
137	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Nest** (<kbd>⌘G</kbd>). See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
138	
139	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
140	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
141	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to group, at least one. |
142	| `name` | string | No | What to call the group. Left out or blank, `Nest <n>`. |
143	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
144	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
145	
146	The clips move whole, keeping their ids, settings, actions, transitions, relative times and stacking, with the earliest starting at 0 inside the nest. A linked partner on an unlocked track goes in with its clip. The nest clip lands on the front-most track the clips were on, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. If those tracks include a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), it lands on the front-most track that isn't one, or the front-most track when all of them are.
147	
148	The nest's canvas is fixed at the project's current size, so a later `set_canvas` can't re-lay out what's inside.
149	
150	**Answers** `new_clips`, which is the nest clip, and `new_tracks`, the nest's own tracks. `get_project` lists the group under `nests`, and the nest clip's `source.project` gives its id, which is what `scope` takes.
151	
152	**Won't run** when:
153	
154	- The clips include an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), which can't go inside a nest.
155	- The nest clip would overlap something unselected by more than the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
156	- It would pass 64 tracks, counting the nest's own, or eight levels of nesting.
157	
158	`clips` holding only a clip that's already a nest changes nothing. An empty list or an unknown clip id is an error.
159	
160	## `unnest`
161	
162	Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes.
163	
164	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>). See [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest).
165	
166	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
167	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The nest clip to open. |
169	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
170	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
171	
172	It's the inverse of `nest`, apart from the ids, which are all fresh. Clips land at the nest clip's start plus their own, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's own, and missing tracks are added behind it. A clip the overlap rule won't allow goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped.
173	
174	A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents gives all of them back, because trimming a nest hides what's inside and doesn't cut it. When another clip still shows the same nest, the nest stays for that clip.
175	
176	**Answers** `new_clips`, the returned clips, and `new_tracks` when any were added.
177	
178	**Won't run** on a clip that isn't a nest, which is an error.
